question: Gopal invests a sum of ₹ 5400 and Akshay invests a sum of ₹10200 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 4 years, Akshay gets ₹720 more interest than Gopal, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Extra principal invested by Akshay = ₹10200 − ₹5400 = ₹4800

Extra interest earned in 4 years = ₹720 ⇒ Extra interest for 1 year = 720 ÷ 4 = ₹180

Rate of interest = (1 Year Interest ÷ Extra Principal) × 100

Rate = (180 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 3.75%

**∴ The correct answer is 3.75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Gopal's Principal (P₁) = ₹5400

Akshay's Principal (P₂) = ₹10200

Time (T) = 4 years

Difference in SI = ₹720

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
